question: The Community of Madrid Youth Council plays a key role in representing young people and their organisations in the democratic life of the region. Its disbanding limits the ability of Madrid’s young people to participate in decision-making.

The measure goes against the European Commission’s objectives, as set out in Article 165 TFEU and the EU youth strategy (2019-2027), which promote the active participation of young people in democratic life in Europe.

Following the European Year of Youth 2022, the Commission has strengthened its commitment to giving young people a voice in decisions that affect them, which highlights the conflict between EU policies and this regional decision. In light of the above: 1.
What is the Commission’s view on how disbanding this youth council might go against the objectives of Article 165 TFEU and the EU youth strategy (2019-2027)?
What steps will the Commission take to ensure that public spaces for participation are not taken away from young people in regions such as Madrid?
In the context of the ‘youth check’, what actions can the Commission take to ensure that regional decisions respect youth participation commitments?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.1.2025) The EU supports, complements, or supplements the actions of the Member States in youth policy (Article 6 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU)1). This excludes the harmonisation of national laws and regulations (Articles 165 and 166 TFEU). The decision to disband the Madrid youth council is a national competence.

The Commission promotes youth participation through, inter alia, the EU Youth Strategy2 and its instruments. Support for youth participation and for civil society is available through Erasmus+3 and the European Solidarity Corps4.

The Commission fully supports the principles laid out in the Council Resolution on encouraging political participation of young people in democratic life in Europe5, including the need to establish, implement or further develop national, regional and/or local strategies, programmes, structures or other relevant mechanisms for enhancing the political participation of all young people.
The youth check only applies to policy initiatives of the Commission6.
